correctness.rationale: Every source-parent pair has a unique greedy leftmost embedding of the received word. The intervening complementary-bit blocks factor under the 11 prohibition into \(t^r(1+t)^{m-2k+r+1}/((1-t)^k(1-t-t^2))\), with a nonnegative exponent because the k-r one-runs require at least k-r-1 separating zeros. The coefficient criterion proves feasibility and unique-parent equivalence for all m,d. Stars-and-bars gives the entire parameter-class histogram, a two-state transfer matrix gives the double generating series, and the unique dominant root of \(1-z-z^2\) gives the stated fixed-d asymptotic. An independent enumeration in verify.py checked 3,066 cases; its finite coverage is not treated as proof.

value.rationale: A deletion-channel receiver needs the number of admissible distinct source strings, rather than the number of deletion masks. This result supplies that cardinality for every target and arbitrary deletion count and compresses its dependence to just weight and adjacent-11 count. It additionally enumerates every list-size class and exactly identifies all singleton and feasible outputs, with a sharp asymptotic recovery fraction. These are motivated complete channel invariants, not a small-number table or a relabeling of unrestricted counting.
